subject: math.OA
name: Kadison’s similarity problem
statement: For every unital C*-algebra A, is every bounded unital algebra homomorphism π:A→B(H) similar, by an invertible operator on H, to a *-homomorphism?
importance: It asks whether bounded algebra representations automatically respect the Hilbert-space structure after a change of coordinates.
status_note: Nuclear algebras and several other classes have affirmative results; arbitrary C*-algebras remain open.

references.title: Pisier, Similarity Problems and Completely Bounded Maps

subject: math.OA
name: Universal coefficient theorem problem
statement: Does every separable nuclear C*-algebra satisfy the Rosenberg–Schochet universal coefficient theorem relating KK-theory to homomorphisms and Ext of its K-groups?
importance: A positive answer would remove a major structural hypothesis from the classification of nuclear C*-algebras.
status_note: The UCT is known for the bootstrap class and many concrete algebras; separable nuclearity alone is the unresolved scope.

references.title: The UCT problem for nuclear C*-algebras

subject: math.OA
name: Blackadar–Kirchberg quasidiagonality problem
statement: Is every separable unital nuclear stably finite C*-algebra quasidiagonal?
importance: It asks whether all such algebras admit finite-dimensional operator approximations and underlies classification by finite models.
status_note: Major positive results assume the UCT or additional trace hypotheses. Arbitrary separable nuclear stably finite algebras are the open scope.

references.title: Tikuisis, White and Winter, Quasidiagonality of nuclear C*-algebras

subject: math.OA
name: Free group factor isomorphism problem
statement: Are the group von Neumann algebras L(F₂) and L(F₃) isomorphic as von Neumann algebras?
importance: It tests whether free-group rank survives passage from groups to their operator algebras.
status_note: The free group factors are fundamental examples of nonamenable II₁ factors; available invariants do not decide this isomorphism question.

subject: math.OA
name: Single-generator problem for II₁ factors
statement: Is every II₁ factor with separable predual generated as a von Neumann algebra by one operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators?
importance: It asks how much operator data is needed to describe an arbitrary finite factor.
status_note: Many classes are singly generated, but separable predual alone is not known to suffice.

references.title: Popa, Tight decomposition of factors and the single generation problem

subject: math.OA
name: Dixmier’s unitarizability problem
statement: If every uniformly bounded representation of a discrete group G on a Hilbert space is similar to a unitary representation, must G be amenable?
importance: It seeks an operator-theoretic characterization of group amenability.
status_note: Amenable groups are unitarizable, and many nonamenable groups are known not to be; the converse for all discrete groups remains open.

subject: math.OA
name: Kaplansky’s zero-divisor conjecture over ℂ
statement: For every torsion-free discrete group G, is the complex group algebra ℂ[G] free of nonzero zero divisors?
importance: It asks whether torsion-free group structure prevents algebraic cancellation in finitely supported convolution operators.
status_note: The conjecture is known for many group classes. Counterexamples to the separate unit conjecture do not disprove this zero-divisor assertion.

subject: math.OA
name: Strict comparison implies Jiang–Su stability
statement: For every infinite-dimensional simple separable unital nuclear stably finite C*-algebra A, does strict comparison of positive elements by traces imply A ≅ A⊗Z, where Z is the Jiang–Su algebra?
importance: This is the remaining structural implication connecting order, regularity, and classification in the Toms–Winter program.
status_note: Many additional hypotheses give the implication. The statement does not assert that the already established equivalence with finite nuclear dimension is unresolved.

references.title: Castillejos, Evington, Tikuisis and White, Uniform property Gamma

subject: math.OA
name: Single-commutator problem in finite factors
statement: For every II₁ factor M with normalized trace τ and every x∈M with τ(x)=0, do there exist a,b∈M such that x=ab−ba?
importance: It asks whether the trace is the only obstruction to expressing an operator as one commutator.
status_note: Trace-zero elements are sums of finitely many commutators, and single-commutator results cover special cases; the general one-commutator problem is open.

references.title: Dykema and Skripka, On single commutators in II₁-factors

subject: math.OA
name: Naimark’s problem in ZFC
statement: Does ZFC alone prove the existence of a C*-algebra having exactly one irreducible representation up to unitary equivalence but not isomorphic to compact operators on any Hilbert space?
importance: It probes how much set-theoretic dependence is inherent in the structure of nonseparable operator algebras.
status_note: No separable counterexample exists. The diamond principle gives nonseparable counterexamples; whether the unrestricted existence assertion follows from ZFC remains open.

references.title: Akemann and Weaver, Consistency of a counterexample to Naimark’s problem
Banach space theoretical construction of (primitive) spectra of C*-algebras and the Naimark problem revisited
